title: World Models in Pieces: Structural Certification for General Agents
claim: Agents are competent only on certified local pieces, and planning succeeds by routing through them, unlike universal guarantees requiring uniform accuracy.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, jagged puzzle pieces versus clean tiling with red X
description: The figure has two panels. The left panel, titled 'General Agents', shows a fractured jigsaw-like map of colored blocks (blue, green, orange, yellow, magenta) separated by gray noisy texture. The colored blocks are certified pieces with low error, and the gray regions are uncertified with high error. A glowing green arrow labeled 'Long-horizon Planning' weaves through the colored blocks. Labels on the left mark 'Certified Pieces Cert(s, a, s')'. The right panel, titled 'Universal', shows a clean, gap-free rectangular tiling of the same colors, crossed out by a large red X. This implies that universal accuracy is unattainable. A bottom legend maps the four-color swatch to 'Certified/Low Error δ' and the gray texture to 'Uncertified/High Error δ'. The eye goes first to the large colorful puzzle and the green arrow.
caption: World Models in Pieces. The capability of a general agent is localized to specific certified pieces (colored blocks) with some low error $\delta$ (see Definition [ref]) where its internal model provably aligns with reality. Reliable long-horizon planning (green arrow) succeeds by navigating these certified transitions rather than requiring global accuracy.
abstract: In the big-world regime, agents cannot be universally capable and their ability is inevitably specialized across a world model in pieces. Consequently, standard uniform guarantees fail to distinguish between the understanding of critical bottlenecks and irrelevant failures. We first formalize this limitation by proving that general agents are not universal, rendering standard worst-case analysis uninformative. To overcome this, we introduce structural certification, a transition-local framework that maps bounded goal-conditioned performance to entry-wise guarantees on the agent's internal world model. Our main contribution is constructive. We provide algorithms that filter specific transitions using deep compositional goals and prove that a general agent on these goals has a structural world model with a $\mathcal{O}(1/n) + \mathcal{O}(Î´)$ error bound. Conversely, this bound is tight in the small-$Î´$ regime, whose existence is explicitly guaranteed by our certification. These results enable the certifiable deployment of general agents by localizing the specific transitions where long-horizon planning is reliable.
